name: Autosomal Recessive Generalized Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex

criteria.description: Generalized blistering of the skin with onset in infancy or early childhood, predominantly on hands and feet
Intraepidermal cleavage demonstrated by skin biopsy with immunofluorescence mapping
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in KRT14 or KRT5 genes consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Consanguinity or affected siblings supporting autosomal recessive inheritance
Ultrastructural evidence of cytolysis within basal keratinocytes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of generalized blistering with histopathological confirmation of intraepidermal cleavage and identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in KRT14 or KRT5
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, and genetic data due to phenotypic overlap with other EB subtypes.

occasional.symptomName: Aplasia cutis congenita on trunk or limbs

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during secondary infections
Mild microcytic anemia on complete blood count
imaging: Not routinely required; imaging may be used to assess musculoskeletal contractures
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in KRT14 or KRT5 genes confirming autosomal recessive inheritance
other: Skin biopsy showing intraepidermal cleavage with immunofluorescence mapping
Electron microscopy demonstrating cytolysis within basal keratinocytes

distinguishingFeatures: Less severe blistering localized to hands and feet
Absence of biallelic mutations in KRT14 or KRT5
Blistering occurs at the level of the lamina lucida
Mutations in genes such as LAMB3, LAMC2, or COL17A1

redFlags: Extensive generalized blistering with rapid progression
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
Development of musculoskeletal contractures or pseudosyndactyly
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2021.
Has C, et al. Epidermolysis bullosa simplex: clinical and molecular aspects. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2020.
Orphanet Report Series: Autosomal recessive generalized epidermolysis bullosa simplex. Orphanet. 2023.
